Bill number: HB1733
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 1774
 By Rose

 HOUSE BILL 1733

 By Moody

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 37;
 Title 39, Chapter 17, Part 3; Title 40; Title 49 and
 Title 55, Chapter 10, Part 7, relative to
 harassment.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 39-17-308(e), is amended by

deleting subdivision (1) and substituting:

 (1) "Bullying" means an act committed by a school employee or student that

 substantially interferes with a victim's educational benefits, opportunities, or

 performance; and:

 (A) If the act takes place on school grounds, at any school-sponsored

 activity, on school-provided equipment or transportation, or at any official school

 bus stop, the act has the effect of:

 (i) Physically harming the victim or damaging the victim's

 property; or

 (ii) Knowingly placing the victim or victims in reasonable fear of

 physical harm to the victim or damage to the victim's property; or

 (B) If the act takes place off school property or outside of a school-

 sponsored activity, is directed specifically at a victim or victims and has the effect

 of creating a substantial disruption to the education environment or learning

 process;

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 39-17-308(e), is amended by adding

the following appropriately designated subdivisions:

 ( ) "School employee" means an employee of a private school, an LEA, a public

 charter school, or other public school;

 ( ) "Victim" means:

 (A) If the act is committed by a school employee, then any student; and

 (B) If the act is committed by a student, then another student;

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-4503(b)(3), is amended by

adding "and school employee" after "each student".

 SECTION 4. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-4503, is amended by adding

the following as a new subsection:

 (e) A teacher or school employee found to have committed an act of

 harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying is subject to dismissal or suspension.

 SECTION 5. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-5-501(7), is amended by adding

the following as a new subdivision:

 (E) Committing an act of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying in

 violation of the school district's policy adopted in accordance with chapter 6, part 45 of

 this title;

 SECTION 6. This act takes effect July 1, 2026, the public welfare requiring it, and

applies to acts committed on or after that date.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill proposes changes to how bullying is defined and handled in schools. It redefines "bullying" as an act by a student or school employee that substantially interferes with a victim's educational benefits, opportunities, or performance. For acts on school grounds, sponsored activities, provided equipment, transportation, or official bus stops, the act must physically harm the victim or their property, or knowingly place them in reasonable fear of such harm. For acts occurring off school property or outside sponsored activities, the act must be directed at a victim and create a substantial disruption to the education environment or learning process. The bill defines "school employee" to include employees of private schools, public charter schools, other public schools, or local education agencies (LEAs). It defines a "victim" as any student if the act is committed by an employee, or another student if the act is committed by a student. Additionally, the bill would make teachers or school employees subject to suspension or dismissal if they commit acts of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying. It also adds the commission of such acts in violation of school district policy as a ground for certain actions under Tennessee Code Annotated Section 49-5-501. If passed, these changes would take effect July 1, 2026, and apply to acts committed on or after that date.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: It redefines "bullying" as an act by a student or school employee that substantially interferes with a victim's educational benefits, opportunities, or performance. For acts on school grounds, sponsored activities, provided equipment, transportation, or official bus stops, the act must physically harm the victim or their property, or knowingly place them in reasonable fear of such harm. For acts occurring off school property or outside sponsored activities, the act must be directed at a victim and create a substantial disruption to the education environment or learning process.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the covered actors, substantial educational interference requirement, covered locations, and distinct harm or disruption conditions.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill defines "school employee" to include employees of private schools, public charter schools, other public schools, or local education agencies (LEAs).
assessments.rationale: Includes all four categories of employers covered by the definition.

assessments.summary_quote: It defines a "victim" as any student if the act is committed by an employee, or another student if the act is committed by a student.
assessments.rationale: Preserves the distinction between student victims of employee acts and other-student victims of student acts.
Does not mention the amendment to Section 49-6-4503(b)(3) adding "and school employee" after "each student." Other references to school employees do not convey this separate amendment.

assessments.summary_quote: Additionally, the bill would make teachers or school employees subject to suspension or dismissal if they commit acts of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying.
assessments.rationale: Identifies the covered employees, all four forms of misconduct, and both sanctions, but omits the condition that the employee be found to have committed the act.

assessments.summary_quote: It also adds the commission of such acts in violation of school district policy as a ground for certain actions under Tennessee Code Annotated Section 49-5-501.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the addition concerning misconduct that violates district policy, but does not identify subdivision (7) as the amendment target or limit the policy to one adopted under Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 45.

assessments.summary_quote: If passed, these changes would take effect July 1, 2026, and apply to acts committed on or after that date.
assessments.rationale: States both the effective date and the prospective applicability to acts committed on or after that date.
